title: Tplyr table module
text: better understand set module can follow example: First load dummy data: Create Tplyr table wrap function. Create build function tplyr table created first step Create output_list passed dv.tables::mod_Tplyr_table Put everything together start app within {dv.manager} ’s also possible add one table module. last step can also add standalone listing module  mod_tplyr_table function, grouping variable levels data may omitted unused factor levels dropped default. ensure levels appear output, even zero counts, explicitly define levels grouping variable factors. ’s example ensure levels ARM variable (including “empty level”) retained table:
code: # load demo data dm <- pharmaversesdtm::dm my_tplyr_fun <- function(dm) {   tab <- Tplyr::tplyr_table(dm, ARM) |>     Tplyr::add_layer(Tplyr::group_desc(AGE, by = "Age (years)")) |>     Tplyr::add_layer(Tplyr::group_count(SEX, by = "Sex")) |>     Tplyr::add_layer(Tplyr::group_count(RACE, by = "Race"))   return(tab) } build_func <- function(tab) {   Tplyr::build(tab, metadata = TRUE) |>     dplyr::mutate(       row_label2 = ifelse(row_label2 == row_label1, "Total (%)", row_label2)       ) |>     Tplyr::apply_row_masks(row_breaks = TRUE) } output_list <- list(   "Demographic" = list(     tplyr_tab_fun = my_tplyr_fun,     build_fun = build_func   ) ) module_list <- list(   "Table" = dv.tables::mod_Tplyr_table(     module_id = "tplyr_table",     output_list = output_list   ) )  dv.manager::run_app(   data = list("My data" = list(dm = dm)),   module_list = module_list,   filter_data = "dm",   filter_type = "datasets" ) # load additional demo data dm <- pharmaversesdtm::dm   # create second tplyr table my_tplyr_fun2 <- function(dm, ae) {   dm_arm <- dm |> dplyr::select(USUBJID, ARM)   ae_arm <- ae |> dplyr::inner_join(dm_arm, by = "USUBJID")      tab <- Tplyr::tplyr_table(ae_arm, ARM) |>     Tplyr::set_pop_data(dm) |>     Tplyr::set_pop_treat_var(ARM) |>     Tplyr::add_layer(       Tplyr::group_count("All subjects") |>         Tplyr::set_distinct_by(USUBJID) |>         Tplyr::set_format_strings(Tplyr::f_str("xx", distinct_total))     ) |>     Tplyr::add_layer(       Tplyr::group_count("Subjects with adverse events") |>         Tplyr::set_distinct_by(USUBJID) |>         Tplyr::set_format_strings(Tplyr::f_str("xx (xx %)", distinct_n, distinct_pct))     ) |>     Tplyr::add_layer(       Tplyr::group_count(AESEV, by = "Adverse event severity") |>         Tplyr::set_distinct_by(USUBJID) |>         Tplyr::set_format_strings(Tplyr::f_str("xx (xx %)", distinct_n, distinct_pct))     ) |>     Tplyr::add_layer(       Tplyr::group_count("Subjects with serious AE", where = AESER == "Y") |>         Tplyr::set_distinct_by(USUBJID) |>         Tplyr::set_format_strings(Tplyr::f_str("xx (xx %)", distinct_n, distinct_pct))     )   return(tab) }  # create secod build function  build_func2 <- function(tab) {   Tplyr::build(tab, metadata = TRUE) |>     Tplyr::apply_row_masks(row_breaks = TRUE) }  # put second table into the output_list output_list <- list(   "Demographic" = list(     tplyr_tab_fun = my_tplyr_fun,     build_fun = build_func   ),   "Adverse Events" = list(     tplyr_tab_fun = my_tplyr_fun2,     build_fun = build_func   ) )  # put everything together  module_list <- list(   "Table" = dv.tables::mod_Tplyr_table(     module_id = "tplyr_table",     output_list = output_list   ) ) # start app dv.manager::run_app(   data = list("My data" = list(ae = ae, dm = dm)),   module_list = module_list,   filter_data = "dm",   filter_type = "datasets" ) # Add additional entry for standalone listings output_list <- list(   "Demographic" = list(     tplyr_tab_fun = my_tplyr_fun,     build_fun = build_func   ),   "Adverse Events" = list(     tplyr_tab_fun = my_tplyr_fun2,     build_fun = build_func   ),   "Listing" = list(     dataset_names = c("dm", "ae")   ) ) # put everything together  module_list <- list(   "Table" = dv.tables::mod_Tplyr_table(     module_id = "tplyr_table",     output_list = output_list   ) ) # start app dv.manager::run_app(   data = list("My data" = list(ae = ae, dm = dm)),   module_list = module_list,   filter_data = "dm",   filter_type = "datasets" ) # Create table function my_tplyr_fun <- function(dm) {   dm <- dm |>     # to preserve all levels     dplyr::mutate(       ARM = factor(ARM, levels = c("Placebo", "Xanomeline High Dose",                                     "Xanomeline Low Dose", "Screen Failure",                                     "empty level"))     )      tab <- Tplyr::tplyr_table(dm, ARM) |>     Tplyr::add_layer(Tplyr::group_desc(AGE, by = "Age (years)")) |>     Tplyr::add_layer(Tplyr::group_count(SEX, by = "Sex")) |>     Tplyr::add_layer(Tplyr::group_count(RACE, by = "Race"))   return(tab) }  # Building the table build_func <- function(tab) {   Tplyr::build(tab, metadata = TRUE) }

title: Event Count module
text: One two levels hierarchy, top-level summary subjects event. Second level hierarchy can collapsed show first level. First level hierarchy can collapsed show subjects event. Grouping group population size (N) displayed across columns table, optional “Total” column. Optionally apply sub-grouping variable events data (e.g. event severity). Event counts percentages displayed, optionally time risk incidence rates can displayed. Events within hierarchy ordered descending event count (totalled across groups). Tables can downloaded Excel (.xlsx) Word (.rtf). supports bookmarking.

title: Event Count module
text: dv.tables::mod_hierarchical_count_table() module uses several arguments following mandatory rest optional. part app creation, app creator specify values arguments applicable. Mandatory Arguments module_id : unique identifier type character module app. subjid_var: common column across datasets uniquely identify subjects. default: “SUBJID” table_dataset_name: dataset contains events per row. example, ADAE pop_dataset_name: dataset contains one row per subject total population. example, ADSL expects one-record-per-subject dataset least containing subjid_var, structure similar https://www.cdisc.org/kb/examples/adam-subject-level-analysis-adsl-dataset-80283806 Refer dv.tables::mod_hierarchical_count_table() complete list arguments description.

title: Event Count module
text: drop-“Options” menu provides following inputs: Event count : Selection one two levels hierarchy variables table (events) dataset, displayed left side table, e.g. AEBODSYS, AEDECOD. Group : Selection grouping variable subject-level population dataset, displayed across top table, e.g. TRT01P. Minimum %: minimum percentage threshold filtering events. Rows percentage subjects (totalled across group categories) threshold removed output. Defaults 0. Total: Checkbox controls whether display “Total” column totalling data group categories. following input also available “Options” menu show_event_group_by module argument set TRUE: Event group : Selection sub-grouping variable table (events) dataset, displayed across top table main grouping, e.g. AESEV. following inputs also available “Options” menu show_time_at_risk_options module argument set TRUE: Event Date: “Date” class (e.g. ASTDT) table events dataset. Events missing dates excluded analysis. Origin Date: “Date” class (e.g. RANDDT) subject-level population dataset. Events occurring origin date excluded analysis. Censor Date: “Date” class (e.g. EOSDT) subject-level population dataset. Events occurring censor date excluded analysis. Time Risk: Checkbox controls whether display time risk incidence rate columns. subject missing origin censor date, time risk calculated subject excluded population count. Note even checkbox unchecked, events still selected based event, origin censor dates, population count affected. Note event group-specified (show_event_group_by module argument set TRUE) time--risk options available.

title: Tplyr table module for DaVinci's module manager — mod_Tplyr_table
text: module_id [character(1)] character string serves unique identifier module. output_list [list(list())] named list defining outputs generated. element list corresponds table listing must named list one following structures: summary tables: tplyr_tab_fun function takes one datasets input returns tplyr_table object. build_fun function takes tplyr_table object returns built table (typically using Tplyr::build()). metadata argument Tplyr::build() needs set TRUE, corresponding listing can shown. listings: dataset_names character vector dataset names required generate listing. names top-level list elements used identifiers outputs. subjid_var [character(1) | NULL] Column corresponding subject ID. Default value 'USUBJID'. default_vars argument listings_server {dv.listings} passed . pagination argument listings_server {dv.listings} passed . intended_use_label argument listings_server {dv.listings} passed . receiver_id argument listings_server {dv.listings} passed . review argument listings_server {dv.listings} passed . title_layout [character(1)] character string defining users can select outputs output_list. Supported values : "dropdown" (default) Renders current interactive title drop-selector. "tabs" Renders horizontal tabsetPanel one tab per entry output_list. Tabs wrap next line many. rest module behavior unchanged.

E.g: foo_UI(id = ns("foo")) ... foo_server(id = "foo") pattern makes easy programmers fall trap modifying one instance string literal "foo" without modifying rest unaware problem bug hit. also easy mistakes uses "foo" identifier uses (text labels, ...) , often case, parameter explicitly named. One easy fix consists using global variables instead plain string literals. case previous example, mean: ID_FOO <- "foo" foo_UI(ns(ID_FOO)) ... foo_server(ID_FOO) simple addition makes purpose ID_FOO clear also fails gracefully ID_FOO instances updated synchronously along codebase. drawback polluting global namespace identifier variables. easily solved creating container constants, purpose pack_of_constants alias. ID <- pack_of_constants(FOO = "foo", BAR = "bar") ID$FOO "foo" ID$BA Error $.pack_of_constants(ID, BA) : Pack constants "ID" contain "BA" pack constants plain named list enforces elements unique, non-null names. tagged S3 object override extraction operators. use checkmate unnecessary, Good Library(TM) module rely anyways
